title: Cap. II: Vasquez enters — thesis: efficacious election from foresight merits
pass_a_gloss: Into the arena first let the Papists come forth: and for all the rest who follow this opinion (for of the sounder ones many do not follow) let Vasquez speak: Who tries to establish this thesis with many arguments, in 1. quest. 23. art. 3. disp. 89. There is no efficacious election of singular persons unto glory from the sole will of God; but each one is elect unto glory from foresight merits, which by God's grace he is about to do. I premise a few things, that the thesis itself may be better understood; then I will set forth and dissolve the adversaries' arguments. Key lemmas: Papistae / Vasques; electio efficax; merita praevisa; 1. q. 23. a. 3. d. 89.
pass_b_english: First into the arena: the Papists. For all who hold this view (many of the sounder sort do not), let Vasquez speak. He tries to prop this thesis with many arguments (on ST 1.23.3, disp. 89): There is no efficacious election of particular persons to glory from God's will alone; each is elect to glory from foresight merits which God's grace will bring about. A few notes first so the thesis is clear; then the adversaries' arguments, stated and dissolved.
source_text: In arenam primo prodeant Papistae: atque pro caeteris omnibus qui hanc sententiam sequuntur (nam ex sanioribus multi non sequuntur) loquatur Vasques: Qui hanc thesin multis argumentis stabilire conatur, in 1. quaest. 23. art. 3. disp. 89. Nulla est electio efficax singularium personarum ad gloriam ex sola Dei voluntate; sed quilibet ad gloriam eligitur ex meritis praevisis, quae Dei gratia est facturus. Pauca praemitto, ut ipsa thesis melius intelligatur, dein argumenta adversariorum proponam & dissolvam.
